pr.title: coverage: Enlarge empty spans during MIR instrumentation, not codegen
pr.description:
This re-lands the part of rust-lang/rust#140847 that was (hopefully) not responsible for the coverage-instrumentation regressions that caused that PR to be reverted.

---

Enlarging empty spans was historically performed during MIR instrumentation, but had to be moved to codegen as part of larger changes in rust-lang/rust#134497, leading to the status quo. But now there should be no reason not to move that step back to its more logical home in instrumentaion.
pr.author: Zalathar

analysis.originalLogic: At coverage MIR instrumentation, `extract_refined_covspans` collects/refines covspans (discarding holes, removing unwanted overlaps), then deduplicates/merges and emits `Code` mappings. In the status quo after rust-lang/rust#134497, empty spans were not enlarged there. Instead, enlargement was deferred to LLVM codegen: `make_coords` called `ensure_non_empty_span`, which tried to widen an empty span over an adjacent `{` or `}`, and returned `None` for spans it could not enlarge. The PR description says enlarging empty spans "had to be moved to codegen as part of larger changes in rust-lang/rust#134497, leading to the status quo."
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historically incorrect placement: letting `InstrumentCoverage` emit empty coverage spans and deferring `ensure_non_empty_span` until codegen map generation. That leaves empty spans in the MIR coverage statements, so adjacent mappings are not merged at instrumentation time, and codegen must silently drop or widen them later. The re-land moved the step back into instrumentation: after overlap removal and before merge, `covspans.retain_mut` either enlarges each empty span or discards it ("For all empty spans, either enlarge them to be non-empty, or discard them."), then merges with `covspans.dedup_by(|b, a| a.merge_if_eligible(b));`. Codegen then asserts the invariant instead of repairing it: `debug_assert!(false, "can't make coords from empty span: {span:?}"); return None;`.
analysis.inputDomain: Coverage-instrumented Rust functions whose refined coverage spans can be empty, especially spans at block/arm boundaries next to braces (closing braces, end of async closure bodies, match arms). Spans are byte positions in a single source file, and enlargement only applies when the adjacent source byte is ASCII `{` after the span or ASCII `}` before it. The examples in the patch are async closures and match arms, including `instrument_coverage_cleanup.rs` spans such as `15:2: 15:2`.
analysis.summary: For coverage instrumentation, empty spans must be enlarged (over an adjacent ASCII `{`/`}`) or discarded during the InstrumentCoverage pass, before dedup/merge, rather than deferred to LLVM codegen. Doing it in instrumentation lets adjacent mappings merge and leaves codegen with a strict non-empty-span invariant. The MIR and cov-map test expectations change accordingly, and the enlarged spans remain visible after CleanupPostBorrowck.
analysis.trigger: A coverage-instrumented function produces an empty refined coverage span, and `ensure_non_empty_span` is applied at the wrong pipeline location (codegen) instead of during InstrumentCoverage before span merging.
preconditions: Coverage instrumentation is enabled for the function.
The source map is available for `span_to_source`.
Enlargement is possible only when `src.as_bytes().get(end) == Some(b'{')`, or `start > 0 && src.as_bytes()[start - 1] == b'}'`.
pitfalls: Adjusting `BytePos` by 1 is only valid because the checked neighboring character is specifically an ASCII brace; do not generalize this to arbitrary characters.
Enlargement must happen before merge/dedup; otherwise equivalent empty/adjacent spans produce separate mappings that cannot merge.
Un-enlargeable empty spans must be discarded by `retain_mut` rather than passed on.
Once codegen asserts non-empty spans, any new producer of empty coverage spans becomes a debug-build failure, so instrumenting passes must uphold the invariant.
`span_to_source` can fail (`.ok()?`), in which case the empty span is dropped.
analysis.testStrategy: Compare two builds that differ only in where empty-span enlargement happens, using the same coverage test source: (A) defer enlargement to codegen, (B) enlarge/discard inside InstrumentCoverage before merge. Inspect `tests/mir-opt/coverage/*.InstrumentCoverage.diff` and the post-pass `CleanupPostBorrowck` dump: old output has empty-coordinate mappings such as `15:2: 15:2`, new output has widened coordinates such as `15:1: 15:2` and `21:1: 21:2`. Check `.cov-map` output: in `async_closure.cov-map`, the old two mappings per closure become one (`-Number of file 0 mappings: 2` / `+Number of file 0 mappings: 1`), and raw bytes shrink from 14 to 9. Include async-closure and match-arm cases with empty spans at braces. This historical patch was not executed here; no reproduction or compiler run is claimed.
